 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In this story Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves left Wednesday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks with a left heel injury in the third quarter and didn't return.
 Luka Dončić, meanwhile, told reporters postgame that he's "good" after rolling his ankle in the fourth quarter. Head coach JJ Redick classified Dončić's injury postgame as a "tweak."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Per Redick , X-rays on Reaves' heel were negative, but the nature and extent of his injury remained unclear postgame. Reaves is scheduled for further imaging on Thursday. Redick also said the Lakers aren't concerned about it being an Achilles injury.
 Reaves appeared to sustain his injury midway through the third quarter. He limped back on defense after a Lakers turnover and subbed himself out of the game at the end of the Milwaukee possession.
 The Lakers then ruled him out with a left heel injury in the fourth quarter. They held a 114-90 lead with 4:23 remaining in the fourth quarter at the time of his exit and went on to a 123-112 win.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Luka's injury scare
 In the fourth quarter as the Lakers held a 21-point lead, Dončić rolled his right ankle when he landed on Kyle Kuzma's foot after an and-one 3-pointer.
 Dončić remained down on the court in pain for several moments after his injury. He was able to eventually stand up and shoot his free throw, but left for the locker room from there.
 While the news of Dončić escaping serious injury is good for the Lakers, concern remains about Reaves' outlook moving forward.
 Dončić and Reaves have thrived this season as the Lakers' 1-2 punch in the aftermath of LeBron James' exit in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers. Dončić entered Monday as the NBA's leading scorer (39.3 points per game) and is making an early case as the MVP front-runner. He finished Wednesday's game with 32 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Reaves entered Wednesday averaging a career-high 25.2 points, alongside 4.6 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1 steal per game. He tallied 18 points, 5 assists, 3 rebounds and 3 steals in 25 minutes before his early exit.
 The Lakers, meanwhile, are off to an NBA-best 11-2 start with Wednesday's win. They have three days off before a Sunday road game against the Phoenix Suns.
